title: Cascade Rituals and Budget Sparring — All Hands
summary: Company all-hands focused on budget reforecast, hiring cadence adjustments, product and infra tradeoffs, an incident postmortem summary, and updated cadence for cross-team rituals. Leadership debated where to prioritize runway versus hiring velocity and agreed on a conservative hiring pause for non-critical ICs with continued hires for infra and security teams. Action items assigned for a trimmed Q3 plan and a follow-up finance+engineering session.
topics: Q3 budget reforecast and runway scenarios
Runtime performance and KV cache regression
Private deployments momentum and compliance asks
action_items: Owner: Rajiv Kumar; Item: Share two runway scenarios (base / conservative) with team; Due: 2026-07-20
Owner: Omar Singh; Item: Produce 2-page infra cost map and top 3 optimization levers (batching/quantization/routing); Due: 2026-07-23
Owner: Priya Menon; Item: Draft internal hiring communication and updated interview slate; Due: 2026-07-18
Owner: Lena Zhao; Item: Prioritize roadmap slices for trimmed Q3 plan and note customer-impacting features; Due: 2026-07-22
next_steps: Weekly incident retrospective summary to be circulated by Omar next Tuesday
All-hands follow-up doc with deck links and FAQ to be posted in #all-hands channel
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16 09:00 PDT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom / All Hands channel
Deck: LINK: shorturl.at/qBZ18 (exec deck)
Attendees: see metadata

[00:00:00] Asha (CEO): ok, hi everyone, starting at 9 on the dot. Uh, quick housekeeping, we'll run 55, 60 minutes, cover budget reforecast, hiring, infra issues, and an incident note. Marco, quick mic check?
[00:00:12] Marco (CTO): Yep, loud and clear, thanks.
[00:00:18] Asha: Cool. Rajiv from finance is on, he'll walk us through runway options, then we'll go to product and infra.
[00:00:27] Rajiv (Finance): Morning all, thanks, I'll be concise. We ran three scenarios since last week: baseline, conservative, and aggressive. Baseline assumes current spend run rate plus modest hiring; conservative assumes a 15% spending reduction and hires limited to critical roles; aggressive assumes continued hiring to meet roadmap which shortens runway by about four months.
[00:00:50] Rajiv: The key is runway is currently about 13 months baseline, 18 months aggressive if we cut some deferred revenue assumptions, and down to 8 months aggressive if we accelerate hiring without new commitments, sorry, that was messy — um, numbers in the deck.
[00:01:06] Asha: Thanks, that was helpful. Quick Q: what are the biggest levers to hit the conservative plan?
[00:01:12] Rajiv: Top three: slow hiring for non-critical ICs, pause a few marketing campaigns scheduled in Q3, and reduce cloud variable spend via infra optimization — Omar will speak to that.
[00:01:24] Omar (Head of Infra): Yeah, on infra side we have clear levers: batching improvements in the serving runtime, tighter prefix caching, and moving a subset of heavy-observation workloads to quantized variants. There was also the June outage which created some tail costs we'll cover.
[00:01:40] Lena (VP Product): Sorry can I jump in — on batching and caching, we have customer-surface implications. If we push batching more aggressively we risk latency SLOs for the low-latency tier. So tradeoffs.
[00:01:52] Omar: Totally, which is why we want to target non-latency critical workloads first, like async embedding jobs or large-batch exports.
[00:02:00] Speaker 1 (Staff Question): Where does dedicated vs hosted fit in — are we seeing demand for private deploys that justify Dedicated capacity?
[00:02:06] Asha: Good question. Marco?
[00:02:09] Marco: Demand is healthy. We signed three new Private pilots in the last quarter, mostly financial services customers asking for V P C and H S M KMS integrations. They are higher ACV but longer sales cycles; they also exert infra and compliance costs. So revenue per deal is good but we need to weigh margin impact and onboarding headcount.
[00:02:30] Marco: Note: sometimes the transcription engine reads KMS as K M S, so ignore that if it shows up funny in the deck.
[00:02:36] Asha: Right. Ok moving on, incident review. Omar, can you summarize the June 28th outage for folks who missed the postmortem?
[00:02:44] Omar: Sure. On June 28th at ~02:15 UTC we had a cascading failure from a misconfigured autoscaling policy combined with a kernel-level regression in the newer runtime patch. The KV cache eviction threshold was misapplied which caused thrashing on a few nodes, then the scheduler rebalanced and we saw a 12-minute window of increased latency and partial request failures for the dedicated pool in us-west-2.
[00:03:05] Omar: Root cause: a config rollout combined with a regression in tensor-kernel selection that increased memory pressure. Mitigations: rollback, tightened canary windows, and an automated alarm on unexpected eviction rates. Postmortem doc link in the deck.
[00:03:19] Maya (Eng Lead): Was there data loss?
[00:03:20] Omar: No persisted user data lost. Key-value cache is ephemeral. We did see some customer requests failed and we emailed impacted customers within the SLA window.
[00:03:29] Speaker 2 (Engineer): Were the quantized runtime paths involved? The notes say something about quantization edges.
[00:03:34] Omar: Yeah there was interplay with a new quantized kernel that didn't fall back cleanly under pressure. We're adding an extra verification step in CI to simulate eviction pressure.
[00:03:42] Asha: Thanks. I know outages make everyone nervous, but the follow-ups have been solid. Next topic: hiring cadence. Priya?
[00:03:50] Priya (Head of People): Quick status: we opened 34 reqs across the org. Considering runway we propose a selective pause: continue hiring for infra (3 roles), security (2 roles), and critical product hires (4 roles), but pause general IC hiring until we finalize the Q3 plan. We'll publish a FAQ and update the interview panel schedule.
[00:04:12] Priya: We'll also prioritize internal mobility to fill some gaps and reduce external spend.
[00:04:18] Asha: Questions on that?
[00:04:20] Speaker 3 (Sales): Concern: sales has several quota-carrying AE roles that are revenue-critical. Are those considered critical?
[00:04:26] Rajiv: Yes, sales-critical roles will be handled case-by-case; finance will triage with GTM leadership.
[00:04:31] Lena: From product POV, we prefer to keep two PM hires given several large enterprise pilots requiring dedicated program management.
[00:04:38] Asha: So the consensus is a targeted hiring slow-down not a full freeze. We'll finalize decisions after the finance+eng deep-dive next week.
[00:04:46] 
[00:04:50] Asha: Ok, roadmap and cadence — Lena, headline?
[00:04:53] Lena: We're trimming the Q3 roadmap to focus on three customer-facing bets: 1) reliability & SLA hardening, 2) private-deployments onboarding experience (V P C / H S M / S S O flows), and 3) Optimize which model variants we surface in the catalog to reduce mean cost per token. Non-critical exploratory features will be deprioritized.
[00:05:18] Lena: We'll also introduce a weekly cross-functional 30-minute sync for rollout blockers — light touch, invite-only.
[00:05:26] Asha: Ok. Question from chat: are we pausing open-source contributions?
[00:05:30] Marco: Not pausing entirely; we'll reduce dedicated FTE for non-core OSS work and encourage community PRs and sponsorship instead.
[00:05:37] Speaker 4 (Engineer): Any change to partner investments or marketplace listings?
[00:05:40] Asha: We'll hold some channel/partnership spend — Rajiv to flag which ones we can pause without big downstream effects.
[00:05:46] 
[00:05:50] Asha: Quick live demo — Marco, any quick infra metric to show?
[00:05:54] Marco: Sure, sharing screen — sorry demo flakey but I'll overview: request distribution, tail latency percentiles, and batching efficiency.
[00:06:05] [00:06:06] Marco: We saw a 9% regression in p99 for certain long-context workloads after the kernel update — that's part of the regression we rolled back. We're running A/B traffic on older kernel vs new patch in a canary cluster.
[00:06:22] Marco: Also some telemetry mislabels — the KV cache metric sometimes appears as K V cash in dashboards, ignore that, it's a tag mapping issue.
[00:06:29] 
[00:06:34] Speaker 5 (Customer Success): We've been getting some feature requests about per-route cost visibility. Any update?
[00:06:39] Lena: Yes, Redwood Console will add a per-route token cost breakdown in the next release, targeted for late Q3, but we'll prioritize a minimal view for dedicated customers earlier.
[00:06:49] 
[00:06:52] Asha: Ok good. Wrap-up: quick recaps then Q&A. Rajiv, final words?
[00:06:57] Rajiv: Please review the deck offline. We need leadership to sign off on the conservative scenario by Monday so we can publish the hiring guidance.
[00:07:06] Asha: Priya?
[00:07:08] Priya: We'll send the hiring FAQ and updated requisition list today. Please escalate any exceptions to me.
[00:07:14] Lena: I'll surface the trimmed roadmap in the product channel and mark customer-impacting items.
[00:07:20] Omar: I'll post the infra cost levers and schedule the deep-dive for next Wednesday.
[00:07:25] Asha: Great. Open Q&A — please keep it short, we have ~30 minutes left for questions from the floor.
[00:07:33] Speaker 6 (Engineer): On private deployments, are we standardizing our onboarding so that the infra team doesn't become a blocker for every pilot?
[00:07:39] Omar: Yes, we plan to templatize common V P C and K M S flows and provide an onboarding playbook for SEs to reduce bespoke infra work.
[00:07:48] Speaker 7 (Sales Lead): For the pilots signed last quarter, do we have revenue recognition timing changes due to the pause?
[00:07:54] Rajiv: Short answer no immediate hit, but longer sales cycles mean bookings slower to ramp. We'll model case-by-case.
[00:07:59] Speaker 8 (Staff): Hey leadership, will there be a town hall for board-level asks about runway?
[00:08:04] Asha: We'll summarize for the board in the next board packet; no separate town hall planned unless things shift.
[00:08:09] 
[00:08:13] [00:08:13] Asha: Ok thanks everyone. Closing notes: expect the follow-up doc, action items assigned, and the finance+eng deep-dive meeting invite. Good work and keep the focus on reliability and strategic pilots.
[00:08:25] (many people say thanks / clapping emoji in chat)
[00:08:30] Speaker 9 (Staff): quick one — can we have a shorter weekly ops sync instead of the 90-min current one?
[00:08:36] Omar: Yes, we'll trial a 30-min weekly technical unblocker and reduce the longer meeting to biweekly.
[00:08:43] Asha: Good. All right, meeting adjourned.
